# logos nogo checkimports: the unsafe-import filename rule via logos lint at
# original Go and .lgo coordinates. Helper is $GOROOT/lib/logos-nogo;
# behavior only, no source wiring or registry count.
#
# Coverage: a.go importing unsafe (and using it, so no unused-import error)
# fails with nogo::checkimports; the same use in a_unsafe.go is clean; an
# ordinary fmt import with no annotation is clean. The .lgo attack maps to
# the original main.lgo line, never an eject temp; a_unsafe.lgo ejects as
# a_unsafe.go and is clean.
#
# Capability separation: each unsafe fixture carries an explicit
# transitive_unsafe_allowlist for its own module so the capabilities gate
# (deny by default) cannot mask or mimic the nogo::checkimports lint. No
# transitive_unsafe = "allow" waiver is used anywhere. Attack cases assert
# no capabilities:: diagnostic alongside the nogo finding.
#
# .lgo suffix grounding: check_imports.go classifies on the pass.Fset
# filename, which for .lgo packages is the ejected .go path
# (src/cmd/go/internal/work/logos_nogo.go builds srcs from the eject dir and
# maps findings back through the edit map). The compiler eject namer
# (src/cmd/compile/internal/logos/eject.go ejectedName: TrimSuffix(base,
# Ext(base)) + ".go") preserves the stem, so a_unsafe.lgo ejects as
# a_unsafe.go and satisfies the _unsafe.go suffix rule; the edit map carries
# the finding back to the original .lgo coordinates.
#
# Zip gap (recorded, not exercised): PreferredZipImport in
# lib/logos-nogo/internal/checkimports/check_imports.go is explicit opt-in
# with no CLI/config wiring (no reference in
# lib/logos-nogo/internal/flags/flags.go); the default empty disables the
# archive/zip case. This script imports no archive/zip and exercises only the
# unsafe rule. The zip opt-in stays covered by its direct-var unit test; the
# rule and its tests are retained.
env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local

mkdir $WORK/bin

# Go attack: plain a.go importing unsafe fails at its original line.
cd unsafeattack
! logos lint ./...
stderr 'a\.go:3:.*\[nogo::checkimports\]'
stderr 'must end with _unsafe\.go'
! stderr 'eject'
! stderr 'capabilities::'
cd ..

# Go suffix exemption: the same use in a_unsafe.go is clean.
cd unsafeclean
logos lint ./...
! stderr .
cd ..

# Go control: ordinary fmt import with no annotation is clean.
cd fmtclean
logos lint ./...
! stderr .
cd ..

# lgo attack: unsafe in main.lgo fails at the original .lgo line.
cd lgoattack
! logos lint ./...
stderr 'main\.lgo:3:.*\[nogo::checkimports\]'
! stderr 'eject'
! stderr 'capabilities::'
cd ..

# lgo suffix exemption: a_unsafe.lgo ejects as a_unsafe.go, so clean.
cd lgounsafeclean
logos lint ./...
! stderr .
cd ..

# lgo control: ordinary fmt import in .lgo is clean.
cd lgoclean
logos lint ./...
! stderr .
cd ..

-- unsafeattack/go.mod --
module example.com/unsafeattack

go 1.27

-- unsafeattack/logos.toml --
[capabilities]
transitive_unsafe = "deny"
transitive_unsafe_allowlist = ["example.com/unsafeattack/**"]

-- unsafeattack/a.go --
package main

import "unsafe"

var _ = unsafe.Sizeof(0)

func main() {}

-- unsafeclean/go.mod --
module example.com/unsafeclean

go 1.27

-- unsafeclean/logos.toml --
[capabilities]
transitive_unsafe = "deny"
transitive_unsafe_allowlist = ["example.com/unsafeclean/**"]

-- unsafeclean/a_unsafe.go --
package main

import "unsafe"

var _ = unsafe.Sizeof(0)

func main() {}

-- fmtclean/go.mod --
module example.com/fmtclean

go 1.27

-- fmtclean/main.go --
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	println(fmt.Sprintf("%d", 1))
}

-- lgoattack/go.mod --
module example.com/lgoattack

go 1.27

-- lgoattack/logos.toml --
[capabilities]
transitive_unsafe = "deny"
transitive_unsafe_allowlist = ["example.com/lgoattack/**"]

-- lgoattack/main.lgo --
package main

import "unsafe"

var _ = unsafe.Sizeof(0)

func main() {}
